leyend-text-1: The basics of programming apply to all programming languages. To be a versatile developer, you need to understand these fundamental principles of programming. Some languages are created with specific functionalities, philosophies, or logics, and once you grasp that logic, learning a new language becomes much easier. It’s essential to make your code scalable for updates, as new technologies constantly emerge.
leyend-text-2: There are various modules created by other people, and sometimes it’s better to use them. I try to create my own modules, but doing everything on my own can take an eternity.However, when you rely on a module created by someone else or a company, it may disappear or evolve, making your code obsolete. Therefore, I believe programming is a discipline that requires constant learning to avoid becoming obsolete.
Technologies-text: For a developer, knowing and learning technologies is only 50% of the job. The other 50% is applying that knowledge to different projects. Here, I’m going to explain some technologies I know and the level of proficiency I have with them.
Proyects-text: For developers, creating projects is one of the most crucial steps in mastering their craft. While learning programming languages, frameworks, and tools is essential, applying that knowledge to real-world projects is what truly solidifies understanding and improves problem-solving skills.
About-text-1: Hi, I’m Federico Guakinchay, a passionate and curious developer at the start of my journey in tech. I created this page to showcase the skills I’ve learned and the projects I’ve worked on so far. I’m always eager to learn more and take on challenges that push me to think creatively and solve problems.I enjoy building applications that solve real-world problems. My focus is on writing clean, efficient code and constantly improving my understanding of new technologies.
About-text-2: One of my favorite aspects of development is the problem-solving process—especially when I can discover unique solutions to complex issues. I love the satisfaction that comes from breaking down a challenge, understanding it, and coding something that works beautifully. This page represents my journey, and I look forward to expanding it as I continue learning and taking on more ambitious projects
python: Python is a high-level, general-purpose programming language known for its simplicity, readability, and versatility. Python is one of the first programming languages I learned. In this language, I made my first programs, i completed basic exercises and worked with data structures.
js: JavaScript, the language of the web, is the second language I studied in depth. I used Node.js as the runtime environment and created some projects, though I have less experience with it compared to Python.
rust: Rust is a fast programming language known for its memory safety. I began learning Rust out of curiosity and completed a few basic exercises to understand its syntax, but I haven't yet worked on any full projects in Rust.
octave: Octave is a high-level programming language designed for numerical computations and is largely compatible with MATLAB. I used Octave for data science tasks as a free alternative to MATLAB, and I built a few small programs with it.
arduino: Arduino is a low-level programming platform. I learned the basics of Arduino, including using a supersonic sensor in a simple project, but I haven't developed any major projects with it yet.
assembler: Assembler is a low-level language used for direct control over hardware. I wrote a few small programs in assembler using a simulator, focusing on memory usage and control flow for educational purposes.
django: Django is a Python framework for backend development, built on the philosophy of 'don't repeat yourself' (DRY). It uses an ORM to interact with databases, and I have worked with SQLite during development and PostgreSQL in production. I've built a few small projects with Django and Django REST framework, which are some of my more ambitious projects. I chose Django because it’s a complete framework that simplifies tasks like authentication and database management.
React: React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces, focusing on reusable components. I've developed several projects in React.
html: HTML5 (HyperText Markup Language) is the foundation of web pages. I use it to structure my web projects effectively.
css: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) is what I use to style and design my web applications, creating responsive and aesthetically pleasing interfaces.
vite: Vite is a modern build tool and development server designed to provide a faster, leaner development experience for web applications. I prefer using Bun to create Vite projects because it's faster than other options I’ve worked with.
Git: Git is a free, open-source version control system that helps developers track changes and collaborate on code. It allows teams to work on the same project simultaneously without overwriting each other's contributions.
